newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: SOCCER-CZECHS HIT HARD BY INJURIES AHEAD OF QUALIFIER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CZECHS HIT HARD BY INJURIES AHEAD OF QUALIFIER.

text.p: The Czech Republic, already depleted by the loss of two key players, suffered a further blow on Wednesday when two more veterans were ruled out for Sunday's World Cup group six qualifier against Spain.

Czech coach Dusan Uhrin, scrambling to replace midfielders Radek Bejbl who are suspended for yellow cards, and the injured Patrik Berger, was forced to scratch Kaiserslautern striker Pavel Kuka and Racing Strasbourg defender Jan Suchoparek as well due to injuries.
"I will not call up any other players. We have right now exactly 19 players who will be able to travel to Spain on Saturday and I hope nothing else happens to anyone," Uhrin said.
With only four points from four games, the beaten Euro 96 finalists are on the brink of elimination from qualifying for the 1998 World Cup in France as they head into Sunday's match.

Spain lead group six with 16 points, with Yugoslavia second on 15 points from six matches and Slovakia third on 12 points. Only the top team in each group is guaranteed a spot in the World Cup finals.
Kuka, who has been heavily criticised for missing several easy chances in the last two games against Yugoslavia -- both losses -- will be replaced up front by Racing Lens striker Vladimir Smicer.
Sigma Olomouc defender Karel Rada, who last week agreed to join Turkey's Trabzonspor next year, is expected to replace Suchoparek.
Uhrin would not name his probable squad, saying he wanted more time to see how the players still available fitted together.
